exposure: immediate postpartum intrauterine contraceptive device (IPP-IUCD) insertion
outcome: complications of IPP-IUCD (irregular vaginal bleeding, abdominal pain, vaginal discharge, spontaneous expulsions, lost strings)
cohort: 200 patients who had postpartum IUCD inserted within 10 minutes of placental delivery after vaginal delivery or c-section at a hospital in Peshawar, Pakistan.
finding: IPP-IUCD is a safe and effective contraceptive option after both vaginal and c-section insertions, though lost strings were significantly more common after vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Lost strings were significantly more common following vaginal delivery compared with cesarean delivery (14% vs 1%, P=0.0006).
